scope: Proposition 5.1 (Exact interpolation and approximation) of the manuscript “An atomic certificate for triangular-lattice universal optimality” (preprints/An-atomic-certificate-for-triangular-lattice-universal-optimality-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 090 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 83e0d874119abae5), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every α ≥ 1, let z and e be its Gaussian parameter and data vector defined in Sections 3 and 4. Retain the fixed coefficients ci,0, di,0, Ci in (9). There are unique real coefficient lists ui ∈ R20 , wi ∈ ℓ1 (T; R2 ) (i = 1, 2), indexed respectively by the pairs (ci,n, di,n) on f and T, for which the functions Ji = eπhsFi from that construction satisfy J1(n) = Gz(n), J′ 1(n) = G′ z(n), J2(n) = J′ 2(n) = 0 (n ∈ N). Relative to the finite coefficient lists Aie, they obey ∥wi∥1 < 3 · 10−9 , ∥ui − (Aie)f ∥1 < 10−5 (i = 1, 2). (30) The resulting Fi are real radial Schwartz functions with ˆ︁ F1 = F2. Uniqueness concerns these coefficient lists with the prescribed fixed columns, not all radial Schwartz functions with the same interpolation data.
